content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 10: General Wave Properties: Transverse and longitudinal waves, wave parameters (speed v, frequency f, wavelength λ, time period T, amplitude, crest, trough, cycle, wave front, compression, rarefaction), Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) basics, energy transfer by waves, mechanical vs. electromagnetic waves, reflection, refraction, and diffraction. Real-world examples, applications, and problem-solving techniques will be detailed here.]

mcqs.question: Which formula correctly relates wave speed (v), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ)?
mcqs.explanation: Wave speed is the product of its frequency and wavelength.

shortAnswers.question: Differentiate between transverse and longitudinal waves with an example of each.
shortAnswers.answer: [Answer detailing differences in particle motion relative to wave propagation, e.g., light (transverse), sound (longitudinal).]

longAnswers.question: Explain the phenomena of reflection, refraction, and diffraction of waves using diagrams.
longAnswers.answer: [Detailed explanation with diagrams for each phenomenon, possibly referencing ripple tank observations.]

content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 11: Sound: Sound production by vibrating sources, longitudinal nature (compressions, rarefactions), necessity of a medium (bell-in-jar), speed of sound in different media and factors affecting it (temperature, humidity), echo and its use, ultrasound and its applications, noise pollution, and timbre. Real-world examples, applications, and problem-solving techniques will be detailed here.]

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the speed of sound?
mcqs.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids due to the close packing of particles.

shortAnswers.question: Explain why sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
shortAnswers.answer: [Answer explaining that sound waves require a medium for propagation as they are mechanical waves.]

longAnswers.question: Describe two medical applications of ultrasound.
longAnswers.answer: [Detailed explanation of applications like sonography/imaging and therapeutic uses.]

content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 12: EM Spectrum: Dispersion of light by a prism, colors of the spectrum (relation to f/λ), rainbow formation, properties of EM waves (same speed in air), main components of EM spectrum (radio, micro, IR, visible, UV, X-rays, gamma rays), and their common applications. Real-world examples, applications, and problem-solving techniques will be detailed here.]

mcqs.question: Which EM wave is used for satellite TV?
mcqs.explanation: Microwaves are used for satellite communication.

shortAnswers.question: List visible spectrum colors by increasing wavelength.
shortAnswers.answer: [Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red.]

content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 13: Geometrical Optics: Laws of reflection, mirror formula, uses of spherical mirrors, laws of refraction, Snell's law, total internal reflection and optical fibers, lens formula, power of a lens, uses of lenses (magnifying glass, camera, projector), microscopes, telescopes, and correction of vision defects. Real-world examples, applications, and problem-solving techniques will be detailed here.]

mcqs.question: Optical fibers work on the principle of:
mcqs.explanation: Optical fibers use total internal reflection.

longAnswers.question: Explain how a convex lens corrects long-sightedness (hypermetropia).
longAnswers.answer: [Explanation and diagram showing light focusing behind retina and how convex lens converges light.]

content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 15: Current Electricity: Electric current, conventional current, potential difference, Ohm's law and limitations, resistance/resistivity, factors affecting R, series/parallel circuits, V-I characteristics, Joule's law, circuit components/symbols, measuring devices (ammeter, voltmeter, galvanometer), AC, hazards/safety (fuse, circuit breaker, earth wire). shortAnswers.question: State Ohm's Law and one limitation.
shortAnswers.answer: [V=IR, if temp constant. Limit: non-ohmic conductors.]

longAnswers.question: Explain purpose of fuse and earth wire.
longAnswers.answer: [Fuse: breaks circuit if current high. Earth wire: low resistance path to ground for faults.]

content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 16: Electromagnetism: Magnetic fields, plotting field lines, force on current-carrying conductor (motor principle), uses (relays, bells, speakers), electromagnetic induction, factors affecting induced emf, AC generator, mutual induction, transformers (step-up/down) and uses. Real-world examples, applications, and problem-solving techniques will be detailed here.]

mcqs.question: Device converting electrical to mechanical energy?
mcqs.explanation: Electric motor converts electrical to mechanical energy.

shortAnswers.question: State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
shortAnswers.answer: [Induced e.m.f. ∝ rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.]

longAnswers.question: Explain working of step-up transformer with diagram.
longAnswers.answer: [Mutual induction, primary/secondary coils, Ns/Np = Vs/Vp > 1 for step-up, diagram.]

content.keyPoints: [Key concepts for Unit 17: Electronics: Analog vs. digital, advantages of digital, digital devices, computers as info processing machines, CRO basics, logic gates (NOT, OR, AND, NOR, NAND symbols/truth tables), simple uses of logic gates (burglar alarm). Real-world examples, applications, and problem-solving techniques will be detailed here.]

mcqs.question: Which logic gate outputs HIGH only if all inputs are HIGH?
mcqs.explanation: AND gate outputs 1 if all inputs are 1.

shortAnswers.question: Draw symbol and truth table for a NAND gate.
shortAnswers.answer: [Symbol and truth table (Output 0 only if all inputs 1).]

longAnswers.question: How can a simple burglar alarm be made using logic gates?
longAnswers.answer: [Explanation using sensor and NOT/other gates to trigger alarm.]
